REASONING:
Step 1 – Project framing  
- **Objective:** Enhance climate‑resilient transport connectivity and agricultural market access in selected areas of Sierra Leone.  
- **Scope & Components:** (1) Resilient Urban Transport (US$17 m); (2) Resilient Rural Bridges & Link Roads (US$44 m); (3) Resilient Agriculture Market Infrastructure (US$8 m); (4) Project Management Support (US$5 m); (5) Contingent Emergency Response Component (CERC – US$0).  
- **Delivery model:** IDA grant (US$74 m) administered by the Ministry of Transport and Aviation (MTA) through a Project Coordination and Implementation Unit (PCIU) and overseen by a National Project Steering Committee (NPSC).  
- **Timeline:** Expected approval 29‑May‑2024; expected closing 31‑Dec‑2029 (≈5 years).  
- **Budget:** Total operation cost US$74 million, fully financed by IDA.  
- **Key stakeholders:** GoSL (MTA, SLRA, SLPTA, MoF, MAFS), World Bank, development partners (EU, KfW, GIZ, AfDB, AFD, IFAD, FAO), private sector (bus operators, contractors, market traders), NGOs and women’s groups.  
- **External dependencies:** Climate‑change trends (floods, landslides, extreme heat), successful financing of the SCADeP bridge gap, procurement capacity, private‑sector lease‑operate‑own financing for buses.

Step 2 – Category sweep (candidate risks with supporting text)  

| Category | Candidate risk | Evidence (≤25 words) |
|----------|----------------|----------------------|
| technical | Floods/landslides damaging bridges/roads | “Sierra Leone is highly vulnerable to natural hazards… flooding, landslides… climate change expected to exacerbate flooding… bridge, road, and markets damage” (Sec 10). |
| technical | Procurement unit not established on time | “PCIU does not have a procurement unit currently and it will be established and staffed…” (Procurement risk). |
| technical | Limited capacity to use RAMS/BMS | “SLRA continues to build and update the RAMS inventory and has adequate capacity to utilize it” (Critical assumptions) – implies risk if capacity lacking. |
| financial | Funding gap for SCADeP bridge works | “Funding gap of about US$7.1 million… GoSL fiscal stress… will partially address the financial gap” (Comp 2b). |
| financial | High fiduciary risk (FM) | “FM risk before mitigation is ‘High’… insufficient experience of MTA with World Bank FM procedures” (Annex 7). |
| financial | Construction cost overruns | “Construction projects in Sub‑Saharan Africa experienced cost overrun of more than 15 %” (Sec 56). |
| schedule | NPSC not set up within 60 days | “Recipient shall not later than 60 days… establish a National Project Steering Committee” (Legal covenants). |
| schedule | Rainy‑season construction delays | “Civil works… may be suspended due to prolonged rainy season” (Comp 2b). |
| stakeholder | Institutional fragmentation/coordination gaps | “Institutional framework… fragmented and lacks systematic coordination among multiple agencies” (Sec 15). |
| stakeholder | Resistance from informal transport operators | “Private sector is the major provider… informal operators… unregulated” (Sec 3 of Comp 1). |
| stakeholder | Gender‑based harassment in public transport | “CCTV cameras to track and reduce incidences of harassment/violence… SH/SEA action plan” (Comp 1c). |
| political_regulatory | Political polarization affecting commitment | “Country faces… governance challenges and political polarization” (Country context). |
| environmental | Potential non‑compliance with environmental safeguards | “Construction will follow environment‑friendly norms… but risk of non‑compliance” (Sec 2). |
| organizational | Staff turnover in PCIU undermining continuity | “PCIU will recruit… procurement specialist, FM specialist, internal auditor, social specialist” (Implementation arrangements) – risk of loss. |
| external | Private‑sector lease‑operate‑own financing may fall short | “Private sector financing… lease‑operate‑own… covers about 50 % of capital cost” (Private Capital Facilitation). |

Step 3 – Evidence filter  
All listed risks are directly supported by quoted statements; none are removed.

Step 4 – Assessment & mitigation  

| ID | Likelihood (1‑5) | Impact (1‑5) | Justification | Mitigation |
|----|------------------|--------------|---------------|------------|
| R01 | 4 | 5 | Climate trends already causing floods; bridges are critical assets. | Apply climate‑resilient design (higher freeboard, robust drainage), conduct regular post‑construction monitoring. |
| R02 | 3 | 4 | Procurement unit creation is a pre‑condition; delays would stall works. | Fast‑track recruitment, use interim external procurement experts, monitor via STEP. |
| R03 | 3 | 3 | RAMS/BMS are new; staff may lack expertise. | Provide targeted training, embed technical assistance, hire dedicated asset‑management officers. |
| R04 | 3 | 4 | US$7.1 m gap exists; GoSL fiscal stress noted. | Secure additional donor/partner financing, phase bridge works, include contingency. |
| R05 | 3 | 4 | FM risk rated High; MTA lacks experience. | Implement FM action plan (training, manuals, external audits, segregation of duties). |
| R06 | 3 | 4 | Regional evidence of >15 % overruns; sensitivity analysis shows IRR drop. | Use fixed‑price contracts, include cost contingency, rigorous contractor supervision. |
| R07 | 2 | 3 | Legal covenant mandates 60‑day deadline; manageable but critical. | Appoint NPSC members before project effectiveness, define clear terms of reference. |
| R08 | 4 | 4 | Rainy season historically halts works; bridges located in flood‑prone zones. | Schedule critical civil works in dry months, adopt weather‑resistant construction methods, build temporary access roads. |
| R09 | 3 | 4 | Fragmented institutions risk duplicated effort and delays. | Strengthen NPSC coordination role, formal MoUs, joint monthly steering meetings. |
| R10 | 3 | 3 | Informal operators dominate market; may oppose formal bus scheme. | Conduct stakeholder workshops, offer incentives (lease terms, training), integrate operators into formal system. |
| R11 | 2 | 3 | Harassment risk acknowledged; mitigation planned. | Implement SH/SEA action plan, install CCTV, establish hotline, conduct gender‑sensitivity training. |
| R12 | 2 | 4 | Political polarization could affect budgetary support. | Obtain cross‑party endorsements, embed project in national development plans, maintain transparent reporting. |
| R13 | 2 | 3 | Environmental safeguards are required; non‑compliance possible. | Conduct thorough ESIA, monitor via E&S Management Plan, enforce mitigation measures. |
| R14 | 2 | 3 | Recruitment plan exists; turnover risk moderate. | Offer competitive contracts, continuous capacity‑building, maintain detailed handover documentation. |
| R15 | 3 | 3 | Private financing covers only half of bus fleet cost. | Diversify financing (green bonds, donor grants), include performance‑based payments, secure guarantees. |

Step 5 – Consolidation  
All 15 risks are distinct and supported by the appraisal document; they are retained.
